assessments.reasoning: At https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/1.0/legalcode the HTML title, main h1, “CC BY 1.0” label and inline legal-code heading identify the reference. Three contiguous parts cover all 33,717 bytes and report the claim's publisher digest.

The Index's SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7, bytes [533,639), requires an identifiable grant or licence text and edition supported by a controlling source. The surrounding scope expressly includes historical editions.

The 2026-11-26 Index decision at bb181812e5fe13143c236554068f21d7ce34dd1e, bytes [1119,1318), assigns d7b533fd120f46e6aec47e4bed06b9b6, CC-BY-1.0, Attribution 1.0 Generic, cc-by-1-0-generic, sha256:537a2a97f8025bc26924c65799e9290901ed514fa02d75636c53a1f9b27521af, kind license, state active. The UUID matches the claim subject after its e- prefix.

In the opening fine print of the legal-code body, Creative Commons says “DISTRIBUTION OF THIS DRAFT LICENSE DOES NOT CREATE AN ATTORNEY-CLIENT RELATIONSHIP.” This supports the express limitation. It preserves a genuine question about finality without contradicting the observed title or grant wording.

challenge.method: Compared the main heading and legal-code body with the 4.0 International recommendation, site footer, linked deed, draft disclaimer and adjacent BY-NC decision row. Tested whether the admission rule requires proof of a finalized or effective grant.
challenge.results: The body and page heading both name Attribution 1.0 Generic. The recommendation points to a different edition, the footer describes site content, and BY-NC has a different title, text and digest. The admission rule requires an identifiable grant or license text and edition from a controlling source. The publisher supplies all three documentary elements while leaving finality open.

limitations: The draft notice leaves finality and legal effect unresolved. The Index decision concerns documentary lookup after selection. Publisher currency, SPDX deprecation and release authorization require separate evidence.

The SHA-256 identifies the live /legalcode HTML observed at acquisition. Its canonical link points to /legalcode.en. Byte equality, translation, semantic equivalence, downstream grants, project-wide application and redistribution rights remain unverified.
The policy bundle digest was supplied and was not independently recomputed. These findings concern the six specified claims, rather than qualification of a dataset release.
reasoning: Creative Commons presents a legal-code page titled “Attribution 1.0 Generic.” Its body identifies the edition and contains a conditional “License Grant” in §3. This meets the Index criterion for identifying a license text and edition from the controlling publisher. The Index separately assigns the exact reference its active maintenance classification. SCES-1.0 §§1–4 require direct inspection, authority for each proposition, exact revision and scope, six dependency checks, and an adversarial identity challenge.
